name: Kingdom of Greece

areaKm2.note: League of Nations Statistical Year-Book 1939/40, Table 2: Greece 130 thousand km2 (low, mid). world_1938 Greece polygon = 139,209 km2 computed by the pipeline (high). The Dodecanese were Italian.

population.note: OWID population (HYDE/UN) Greece 1940 = 7,310,983 (mid). COW NMC v7 tpop 1940 = 7,319k (high); samlib table (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)) 7.2M for 1940 (low). League of Nations Year-Book 1939/40 estimate xii.1938 = 7,107k; census 1928 = 6,205k.

urbanization.note: Definitions differ. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_history_of_Greece_and_the_Greek_world: the 1928 census counted 45.6% of Greeks in urban or semi-urban places (high; 1920: 36.3%). HYDE 3.5 via OWID (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/urbanization-last-500-years.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true): Greece 1930 = 15%, 1940 = 20% (low, larger towns only). Mid 0.33 = midpoint of the two definitions.

activePersonnel.note: Composite for November 1940, general mobilisation ordered 28 October. Army: 14 infantry divisions x ~14,000 = 196,000 (division size from Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books), MAA 514), 1 cavalry division ~5,000 and 3 infantry brigades ~15,000; corps troops, Metaxas Line garrisons and depots ~60,000; navy 6,300 regulars + 11,000 reservists = 17,300 (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)); air force ~3,250 (~250 officers + 3,000 men, same page). Sum ~296,500 -> mid 300,000. Low = divisions only partly mobilised on 28 October (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War). High = the 450,000-man combat strength the small-arms stocks were built for (MAA 514 via the samlib page); by April 1941 the army had 20 divisions (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War).

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Greek service was 24 months with a long reserve obligation; the veterans of 1912-22 were in their 40s. Men not yet called up in November 1940; reserve classes were drafted through the winter to form 6 more divisions by April 1941.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Everything outside the P roles in the 300,000 composite: artillery (~900 guns), engineers, signals, the pack trains of a mountain army, Metaxas Line fortress artillery, navy 17,300 and air force ~3,250.

mobilizationRatio.note: Reached mobilisation: ~300,000 in November 1940 and 20 divisions (~430,000 with services) by April 1941 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War), of 7.3M population = 0.04-0.06; high 0.07 = 512,000, above the 450,000-man arms stock (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)).

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Triangular divisions (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War); battalion = 58 officers + 1,000-1,100 men, 3 battalions per regiment (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)). 14 divisions x 3 regiments x 3 battalions x ~1,100 = 139,000, plus the 3 brigades (~12,000) = ~150,000. Low = partial mobilisation of 28 October; high = 20 divisions of April 1941.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: most equipment of First World War issue from Belgium, Austria, Poland and France (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War); per regiment 2 65 mm mountain guns, 4 81 mm mortars, 8 heavy and 36 light machine guns (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)); no tanks and 24 AT guns in all.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: 24-month conscription, officers veterans of the Balkan Wars, the First World War and Asia Minor (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)); the army beat the Italian invasion and counter-attacked into Albania (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War).

count.note: Educated guess. Mounted strength of the one cavalry division: two cavalry regiments of four battalions (squadrons) each, a horse artillery battalion and a mounted machine-gun battalion (structure from Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)); squadron sizes not given.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: horse cavalry with rifles and machine guns, 12 guns in the division.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: regular cavalry cadre; used in the Pindus battle.

count.note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War infobox (Clodfelter and army.gr): 940 artillery pieces in October 1940 (high); Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books): about 900 guns (low, mid). 315-320 mortars and 24 AT guns not counted.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: mixed French, Austrian and Skoda guns of 1910s-1920s designs, 9 batteries per division (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War); ammunition down to less than two months by February 1941.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: effective mountain gunnery against Italian columns at Kalpaki and the Pindus (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War).

count.note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War: the Royal Hellenic Air Force had 45 fighters (mid, high); operational at the outbreak 24 PZL P.24 and 9 Bloch MB.151 (low = 33).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: PZL P.24 gull-wing monoplanes and MB.151 against Fiat CR.42 and G.50 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: PZL P.24 squadrons intercepted escorted Italian bomber raids from 2 November 1940 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War).

count.note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War: 24 light bombers (low; operational 11 Blenheim IV, 10 Fairey Battle, 8 Potez 633), 12 Dornier Do 22G torpedo bombers (mid = 36); high adds 28 naval cooperation and 9 reconnaissance aircraft (61). ~65 auxiliary aircraft not counted.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Blenheim IV modern; Battle, Potez 633 and Do 22 obsolescent; spare parts cut off when the suppliers were occupied.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: as fighters.

count.note: AA guns at 4 per battery. Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books) (MAA 514): 24 Krupp 88 mm and 162 Rheinmetall 20 mm and 37 mm AA guns bought in Germany (186 / 4 = ~46); ~190 AA guns in all (mid 48); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War infobox: 270 AA guns (high 68). Low allows for unserviceable pieces.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: modern German guns, but few and concentrated at Athens, Piraeus and Thessaloniki.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: new arm formed 1937-39.

count.note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War: the elderly cruiser Georgios Averof, two modern destroyers (Vasilefs Georgios class), four Italian-built Hydra-class destroyers and four obsolete Aetos-class destroyers = 11 (mid). Low = Averof plus the 6 newer destroyers. High adds the two pre-1914 battleships Kilkis and Lemnos listed by Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books), which the same page rates as of no combat value.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books): by the late 1930s all Greek ships larger than a destroyer had lost combat value; only 2 of 4 ordered destroyers delivered.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: escorted the convoys that moved 80,000 men and 100,000 animals by sea (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)).

count.note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War: fifteen obsolete torpedo boats and about thirty auxiliary vessels; Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books) gives 13 old torpedo boats and 2 MTBs (mid 17 with the MTBs, low 15). High adds the ~30 auxiliaries (minesweepers, tenders).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: 1910s torpedo boats.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: convoy escort and patrol duty throughout the war.

count.note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War and Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books): six old French-built Katsonis-class submarines of the mid-1920s.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: 1920s French boats.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: regular crews from the 6,300 long-service personnel of the navy (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)); boats kept at sea through the war.

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Papagos and the General Staff pre-planned the defence (plans IB, IBa, IBb), shifted the Macedonian divisions to Epirus once Bulgaria stayed neutral and counter-attacked on 14 November (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_Greece_during_World_War_II); later the belated withdrawal from Albania in April 1941. About 1,500 Venizelist officers had been purged (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)).

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75 (national army) and above. Evidence: national war against an invader; Metaxas regime and its opponents rallied; minorities small after the 1923 population exchange.

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75-1.0 (highly motivated). Evidence: Greek reservists drove a larger, better-equipped Italian army back into Albania in winter conditions (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War).

weapons.note: Anchor: 7 (1905) toward 8 (1943). Evidence: Mannlicher-Schoenauer rifles, Hotchkiss and Saint-Etienne M07 machine guns of First World War issue, 81 mm mortars, 65-155 mm Schneider, Krupp and captured Skoda guns (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)).

armor.note: Anchor: 7. No tanks in service in October 1940 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War); value only matters if armour is added.

ships.note: Anchor: 7 (dreadnought era). Evidence: 1911 armoured cruiser Averof, 1930s destroyers, 1920s submarines.

fortification.note: Anchor: 8 = concrete lines (Maginot). Evidence: the Metaxas Line, 21 concrete forts in Eastern Macedonia and Western Thrace (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_Greece_during_World_War_II); field works elsewhere.

logistics.note: Anchor: 7 (railways). Evidence: 600 military vehicles (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War infobox); Epirus supplied by pack animals over few roads; lack of motor transport and pack animals made the April 1941 withdrawal impossible.

communications.note: Anchor: 7 (telephone and telegraph). Evidence: two signal companies per division (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)), little radio.

isr.note: Anchor: 7 toward 8. Evidence: Hs 126 and Potez 25 observation aircraft, cavalry reconnaissance; no radar.

air.note: Anchor: between 7 (1914) and 8 (1943). Evidence: PZL P.24, MB.151 and Blenheim IV monoplanes alongside Breguet 19 and Potez 25 biplanes (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War).

cyber.note: No military computer networks before ~1990 (cyber anchor 9 = 1990 networks).

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID CSV) Greece: 1940 = 3,543 (low, mid), 1939 = 4,205 (high; 1938 = 4,267), 2011 int$.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Global Military Spending Dataset via OWID, Greece: 1939 = 4.73% (low, last peacetime), 1940 = 7.68% (mid), 1941 = 11.35% (high). COW milex 1940 = 62,145 thousand current US$ (1938 30,122).

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Industry share of output. Protected industry grew in the 1930s, 1939 industrial output 179% of 1928 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_history_of_Greece_and_the_Greek_world), but the economy was dominated by agriculture, shipping and trade; tobacco, textiles and food processing led.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - a/s with a = agricultural share of employment (~0.55) and s = grain self-sufficiency (~0.65): 1 - 0.55/0.65 = 0.15. Greece imported a large part of its wheat; the 1941-42 famine followed the blockade of imports. Import-dependent, kept positive per the convention.

annualCohort.note: Educated guess. Men reaching military age (21) per year: the 1919 birth cohort of ~5M people, depressed by mobilisation 1912-22, half male, ~70% survival; refugees of 1922-23 added older men only.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Roads usable by motor vehicles; Epirus and the Pindus were reached by few roads, and the poor land network made sea transport essential (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War).

railKm.note: CHAT railline Greece 1938 = 2,976 km; no line reached Epirus.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Piraeus, Thessaloniki, Patras, Volos, Kavala and Heraklion; ports carried the 80,000 men and 100,000 animals moved to the front by sea (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)).

merchantTonnage.note: GRT to DWT x 1.5 (low x 1.3, high x 1.6). League of Nations Year-Book 1939/40 Table 113 (https://www.istmat.org/files/uploads/49915/09_strany_mira_-_transport_torgovlya_platyozhnyy_balans.pdf): Greece 1,889k GRT in June 1938 (low 2,456k, mid 2,834k); CHAT shipton 1938 = 1,930k GRT (high 3,088k). Greek ships lost while neutral in 1939-40 are not deducted.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Mountain front supplied by pack animals from railheads in Thessaly and western Macedonia and from the ports; 600 military vehicles in all.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Low = 100,000 army animals moved by sea (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)); national stock of horses, mules and donkeys guessed at 0.5-0.9M.

homeDefense.note: 1.3 row: mountain home terrain with a united, mobilised population against an invader (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War); low 1.2 for the open plains of Macedonia and Thrace and the dependence on sea supply.

notes: Snapshot date November 1940: Italy invaded on 28 October, general mobilisation followed and the Greek counter-offensive began on 14 November. Active personnel is a composite of division strengths (14 infantry divisions, 1 cavalry division, 3 brigades), navy and air force (range 250,000-450,000). Equipment from the Greco-Italian War article (infobox citing Clodfelter and army.gr; air and naval order of battle from MAA 514) and a samlib.ru compilation (Temezhnikov) citing MAA 514. The army had no tanks, so no armour role. No production entries: Greece had little arms industry; heavy equipment came from abroad and the suppliers were occupied by 1940 (Greco-Italian War article). Weakest values: P-role split, trained reserves, food surplus, roads and animals (educated guesses). Ship convention per SOURCES.md: cruiser and destroyers ships_major, torpedo boats and auxiliaries ships_minor.
